track: Net-new prospects: acquisition and after a demo request
track_strategy: This is the campaign's first cold-reader argument: accumulated A/V handoffs, consolidation proof, a short product view, then the platform-and-team invitation. It deliberately uses different property scenes from Prospect Pulse so the same person can enter long-term nurture later without hearing the acquisition sequence again.
open_questions: Confirm the named LUCI lead used for all four acquisition emails sent through Marketing.
Confirm the approved project count and proof URL for [APPROVED PROOF POINT] and [PROOF URL].
Confirm [FEATURE HIGHLIGHT REEL URL] and [BOOKING URL].
Confirm whether Mike or Mark owns each demo request and sends NET-DEMO-02 personally.
Confirm whether ActiveCampaign keeps #Name# or maps it to the production first-name field.

emails.title: The operational problem
emails.sender: Marketing, from the same named LUCI lead
emails.audience: Cold operations, IT, A/V, F&B and entertainment, and marketing leaders at casinos, resorts, and venues
emails.primary_message: Routine A/V changes become relay races when separate controls, vendors, and workarounds own different parts of the room.

strategy.what_why: Open the acquisition sequence with a screen change the reader recognizes, then name the accumulated handoffs behind it.
strategy.for_whom: Leaders who inherit separate room controls, vendor contacts, and workarounds but may not know LUCI.
strategy.reach: Send from a named LUCI lead through Marketing. Keep the body compact, use no asset, and ask for one low-effort reply.
strategy.impact: Put a ticket-window source change in the scene, then define LUCI only after the handoff problem lands.

directions.name: Ticket-window relay
directions.summary: The selected direction, revised for whole-campaign consistency.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

At the ticket window, switching the display from daily hours to event-entry instructions should not require three logins, two calls, and a workaround saved in a notes app.

Separate controls turn a routine request into a relay race. Everyone knows the next guest will arrive before the handoffs finish.

LUCI orchestrates a property's A/V from one interface, so staff can change screens and sources without tracing which system owns each step.

Reply with the A/V task that takes more handoffs than it should.

directions.name: Wrong wall
directions.summary: Open on the moment a wall shows the wrong content before guests arrive.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

The wall is showing the wrong feed, doors open soon, and the first question is not how to fix it. It is which control, vendor, or workaround owns the problem.

That is the tax of separate A/V systems: more handoffs before anyone touches the screen.

LUCI runs a property's A/V from one interface, bringing rooms, sources, and controls into the same operating view.

Reply with the screen change that creates the longest phone tree.

directions.name: Count the steps
directions.summary: Ask the reader to count what sits between a request and the room.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

Pick one ordinary A/V request: move the game, reset the ballroom, change the lobby wall. How many interfaces, calls, and workarounds sit between the request and the room?

The burden comes from everything the environment accumulates around the hardware.

LUCI brings a property's A/V into one interface, so staff work from one view instead of tracing the request across separate systems.

Reply with the task that has collected the most steps.

emails.why_won: It starts in property life, gives the email one dry human observation, and defines LUCI after the problem lands. The r3 final removes the repeated bartender and wrong-wall scenes.

subject_lines.text: How many steps does one display change take?
The ticket window needs a faster answer
When A/V becomes a relay race

emails.preheader: One ticket-window display can expose every extra interface and handoff.

emails.title: Consolidation proof
emails.sender: Marketing, from the same named LUCI lead
emails.audience: Cold net-new prospects who received NET-ACQ-01 and have not replied, booked, or entered an active sales conversation
emails.primary_message: One approved property count shows how LUCI brings varied rooms and hardware into one operating interface.

strategy.what_why: Move from a familiar problem to concrete proof, using one approved count and one destination.
strategy.for_whom: Operations and IT leaders who need evidence that consolidation can work across varied A/V hardware.
strategy.reach: Send five days after NET-ACQ-01 from the same sender. Put the approved count first and use the proof URL as the only CTA.
strategy.impact: Make a mixed-era back-of-house rack the practical consequence of a shorter operating list.

directions.name: Count before claim
directions.summary: The selected direction, revised for whole-campaign consistency.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

What does consolidation look like after the diagram?

At one operating property: [APPROVED PROOF POINT]. LUCI brings those screens, rooms, and controls into a shared operating view while the underlying hardware stays varied.

In the back-of-house rack, equipment can still come from several eras. Staff should not inherit a different control path for each one.

That is the practical proof: fewer paths and handoffs between the request and the room.

See the consolidation proof: [PROOF URL]

directions.name: Ballroom reset
directions.summary: Use a room turnover to turn consolidation into an observable workflow.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

A ballroom flips from a general session to dinner. Screens, sources, and audio all need to move together, but the equipment behind them may come from several eras.

LUCI runs that varied A/V from one interface. At one property, the scope included [APPROVED PROOF POINT].

Staff get one path through the change instead of a scavenger hunt across controls and contacts.

See how the operation came together: [PROOF URL]

directions.name: Keep the hardware mix
directions.summary: Answer the concern that a consistent operation demands uniform equipment.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

A consistent A/V workflow does not require identical hardware in every room.

LUCI brings varied equipment into one operating interface. One approved project makes the scale concrete: [APPROVED PROOF POINT].

The useful result is not another device. It is a bartender, banquet manager, or technician following the same path to the screen.

Hardware can vary. The hunt for the right control should not.

See the consolidation proof: [PROOF URL]

emails.why_won: It gives proof before interpretation and turns hardware variety into a back-of-house operating point. The r3 final removes the repeated ballroom changeover.

emails.title: Recorded walkthrough
emails.sender: Marketing, from the same named LUCI lead
emails.audience: Cold net-new prospects who received the first two acquisition emails and have not entered a sales conversation
emails.primary_message: A short reel shows how New LUCI gives staff more direct control of room changes, screen checks, maps, and activity history.

strategy.what_why: Show the product only after the reader understands the problem and proof, using the shortest visual asset.
strategy.for_whom: Busy venue leaders who want to see the workflow before considering a meeting.
strategy.reach: Send five days after NET-ACQ-02. Define LUCI and New LUCI in one line, then use the feature reel as the sole CTA.
strategy.impact: Follow one access-and-control sequence without borrowing another property's scene or the ballroom's staging workflow.

directions.name: Access in sequence
directions.summary: The selected direction, revised for whole-campaign consistency.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

New LUCI is in beta on a faster foundation, giving staff more direct control over rooms, maps, activity, and access.

The short reel follows one access sequence: sign in, open only the controls approved for the room, adjust grouped audio, review the activity record, and end the session.

Access should be clear before anyone touches a control.

Watch the feature highlight reel: [FEATURE HIGHLIGHT REEL URL]

directions.name: Bartender view
directions.summary: Show how approved controls and live screen checks simplify one shift.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

LUCI brings a property's A/V into one interface. New LUCI is its beta update, giving staff more direct control on a faster, more responsive foundation.

In the short reel, a bartender opens only the controls approved for that space, checks what a screen is actually playing, and changes the room without searching the building for help.

The screen gets the attention. The control hunt does not.

Watch the feature highlight reel: [FEATURE HIGHLIGHT REEL URL]

directions.name: Map to wall
directions.summary: Use the live map and screen view as the visual thread.
directions.draft:

LUCI runs A/V across a property from one interface. New LUCI is the beta version that adds more direct control over the map, room views, activity, and access.

Watch the feature highlight reel: [FEATURE HIGHLIGHT REEL URL]

emails.title: Platform, team, and invitation
emails.sender: Marketing, from the same named LUCI lead
emails.audience: Cold net-new prospects completing the acquisition cycle without a reply, booking, or active opportunity
emails.primary_message: LUCI brings varied A/V into one interface and keeps a team monitoring, diagnosing, and supporting the environment.

strategy.what_why: Close the acquisition cycle by pairing the platform with the people who remain accountable, then offer a focused demo.
strategy.for_whom: Operations and IT leaders who understand the problem and product but still need confidence in the continuing relationship.
strategy.reach: Send five days after NET-ACQ-03 from the same sender. Use the booking URL as the only CTA.
strategy.impact: Make the Monday-morning work of monitoring and diagnosis more concrete than a generic partnership promise.

directions.name: Monday morning
directions.summary: The selected direction, revised for whole-campaign consistency.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

Different rooms can keep different hardware. Staff should not need different operating habits for each one.

LUCI standardizes the operating path across those rooms. If an endpoint fails, the LUCI team receives an alert and sees device context and logs before the support conversation begins.

Software can earn the meeting. Accountability has to stay after it.

That continuing work matters: we've never lost a client.

If fewer interfaces and handoffs are on your list, book a focused demo: [BOOKING URL]

directions.name: Map and people
directions.summary: Pair a shared property map with the people watching the environment.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

LUCI runs a property's A/V from one interface, giving staff one map for rooms, screens, and sources even when the equipment varies behind it.

The same view helps the LUCI team monitor the environment, diagnose issues, and support the people on site. A shared screen is useful. Shared accountability is the part that survives a busy Saturday.

If that combination fits an active priority, book a demo built around your property: [BOOKING URL]

directions.name: Focused invitation
directions.summary: Qualify the demo around a current room, screen, or workflow problem.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

A LUCI demo is most useful when there is a specific knot to untangle: a ballroom with too many control paths, a wall nobody can verify remotely, or staff moving between different interfaces.

LUCI brings the property's A/V into one operating interface. Its team continues to monitor, diagnose, and support the environment as needs change.

We will skip the generic tour and start with the knot.

Book a focused demo: [BOOKING URL]

emails.why_won: It makes continuing support concrete and gives the retention line a natural invitation context. The r3 final varies the partnership language through alerts, context, and logs.

emails.title: Immediate confirmation
emails.sender: Marketing on behalf of the assigned sales owner (Mike or Mark)
emails.audience: Net-new prospects who submitted a demo request
emails.primary_message: LUCI received the request, and the prospect can choose a time without reading another pitch.

strategy.what_why: Confirm the request and remove scheduling uncertainty.
strategy.for_whom: Hand-raisers who need logistics, not persuasion.
strategy.reach: Send immediately from a monitored address. Put the booking URL on its own line.
strategy.impact: Keep the tone plain and warm, with one human sentence about calendar friction.

directions.name: Time first
directions.summary: The selected direction, revised for whole-campaign consistency.
directions.draft:

Thanks for asking to see LUCI.

Your LUCI contact will confirm the meeting and shape the walkthrough around any priorities you shared. The note stays short.

Choose a time: [BOOKING URL]

emails.title: Personal follow-up
emails.audience: Net-new prospects who submitted a demo request
emails.primary_message: A real person wants one concrete priority so the LUCI walkthrough starts with the prospect's operation.

strategy.what_why: Show that Mike or Mark saw the request and collect one useful input.
strategy.for_whom: Prospects whose interest is current and who should not receive another campaign summary.
strategy.reach: Send personally the same or next business day. Ask one question and use reply as the sole CTA.
strategy.impact: Offer three recognizable examples and sound like the sender wrote the note in 30 seconds.

directions.name: One thing
directions.summary: The selected direction, revised for whole-campaign consistency.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

I saw your request, and I want the walkthrough to start with your operation rather than a generic tour.

What is the one room, screen, or workflow you want us to cover? One line is enough.

Reply with the priority, and I will build around it.

directions.name: Skip the tour
directions.summary: Promise a focused session instead of a generic product tour.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

I have your request to see LUCI, the platform that brings a property's A/V into one interface.

Rather than run every screen in order, tell me where the operation gets stuck. A room reset, a wrong feed, a control nobody wants to touch. I will start there.

Reply with the problem you want the walkthrough to answer.

directions.name: Thirty-second note
directions.summary: Keep the note especially brief and let the reply set the agenda.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

Saw your LUCI request. It runs a property's A/V from one interface, but the useful demo starts with your room, wall, or workflow.

Send me the one thing that should work better. A sentence is plenty; a novel creates more homework for both of us.

Reply with the priority, and I will build around it.

emails.why_won: It reads like a genuine personal note and asks for one useful input. The r3 final removes the repeated bartender, ballroom, wrong-screen, slide-order, and homework material.
